The '''National Institutes of Design''' ('''NID''') is a group of autonomous public design institutes in India, with the [[National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad|first institute]] established in 1961 in [[Ahmedabad]]. The other NIDs are located in the cities of [[Kurukshetra]], [[Amaravati]], [[Jorhat]] and [[Bhopal]]. The NIDs function autonomously under the [[Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade]] (DPIIT), [[Ministry of Commerce and Industry (India)|Ministry of Commerce and Industry]], [[Government of India]]. The NIDs are recognised by the [[Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (India)|Department of Scientific and Industrial Research]] of the government's [[Ministry of Science and Technology]] as a scientific and industrial research organisation. The institutes are accorded the status of [[Institutes of National Importance]] under the National Institute of Design Act, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nid.edu/Userfiles/The_National_Institute_of_Design_Bill.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=3 April 2021 |archive-date=6 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506034347/https://www.nid.edu/Userfiles/The_National_Institute_of_Design_Bill.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-10 |title=NID Coaching - In Ahmedabad {{!}} Pune {{!}} Delhi {{!}} Mumbai {{!}} Lucknow {{!}} Patna {{!}} Ranchi {{!}} Bhanwar Rathore Design Studio |url=https://rathoredesign.com/nid-entrance-exam-coaching/?nid |access-date=2025-08-02 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Institutes ==
The primary institute is located in [[Ahmedabad]] with extension campuses in [[Gandhinagar]] and [[Bengaluru]]. The creation of four additional NIDs was suggested as part of the central government's 2007 National Design Policy.<ref name="toi-1-apr-2012">[https://web.archive.org/web/20131017194407/http://epaper.timesofindia.com/Default/Scripting/ArticleWin.asp?From=Archive&Source=Page&Skin=TOINEW&BaseHref=TOIA/2012/04/01&PageLabel=6&EntityId=Ar00604&ViewMode=HTML "PPP model for new NIDs Nixed". Times of India, Ahmedabad.  Times City section, page 6.  1 April 2012.]</ref><ref name="hindu-19-feb-2011">[http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/article1471990.ece "Centre committed to development of Assam, northeast: Manmohan". The Hindu, 19 February 2011]</ref>

The [[Union budget of India|Union Budget]] 2026-27 prioritizes the burgeoning design sector, addressing the critical talent shortage through strategic expansion. [[Finance minister of india|Finance Minister]] [[Nirmala Sitharaman]]’s proposal for a new '''National Institute of Design''' in [[Eastern India]] marks a pivotal shift in regional development. This initiative reinforces the national design vision, integrating the East into a high-caliber institutional framework dedicated to professional excellence and innovation.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Das |first=Tina |date=1 Feb 2026 |title=Sitharaman proposes a new National Institute of Design in eastern India |url=https://theprint.in/economy/sitharaman-national-institute-of-design-eastern-india/2843128/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260408111946/https://theprint.in/economy/sitharaman-national-institute-of-design-eastern-india/2843128/ |archive-date=8 Apr 2026 |access-date=1 Feb 2026 |work=[[ThePrint]] 01 February, 2026 10:27 pm IST |location=[[New Delhi]]}}</ref>

== Admissions ==
The NID Design Aptitude Test (NID-DAT) is a two-stage national-level entrance examination for the National Institutes of Design (NIDs), organized annually by the NID Admissions Cell for admissions to undergraduate and postgraduate courses at these institutes. The first stage of the examination is the NID-DAT Prelims, which consists of a pen-and-paper design and general aptitude test. The second stage is the NID-DAT Mains, which typically includes an in-studio design test and may also feature a personal interview. The tests aim to evaluate candidates' visualization skills, creativity, observational abilities, knowledge, comprehension, and analytical skills, among other competencies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NID Admission: 2019-20|url=http://admissions.nid.edu/NIDA2019/Default.aspx|access-date=2019-08-06|website=admissions.nid.edu}}</ref>

== Academics ==
The courses available at NID span a wide range of disciplines (like graphic design, product design, interior design, filmmaking, animation, etc.) and include Bachelor of Design (B.Des.), Graduate Diploma Program in Design (GDPD), Master of Design (M.Des.) and doctoral programs (PhD). Several international programs and foundation courses are also available.{{Citation needed|date=April 2021}}
